newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-Pioneer mulls exit from Ampol.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-Pioneer mulls exit from Ampol.

text.p: Building products and petrol refinery group Pioneer International Ltd said on Wednesday it was considering selling its half of the Ampol petrol refining and marketing joint venture with Caltex Australia Ltd.
"The company has appointed the investment banks J.P. Morgan and Macquarie Bank to assist it with its review, which it expects may take several months to complete," Pioneer said.
The announcement overshadowed a weaker earnings report from the group, whose half year net profit fell by 16 percent to A$112.7 million compared with the previous first half.
"Our growth really needs to be core businesses of concrete and quarries and cement into tied markets," managing director John Schubert told reporters.
"We will add most value to our shareholders by concentrating quite narrowly on our product focus but having a broad geographic focus," Schubert said.
Pioneer's review of the Ampol investment began last month and was partly triggered by the investment's unsatisfactory return on shareholders funds, Schubert said.
Schubert said the company would only sell its stake if the price received added value to the company for its shareholders.
"We are not setting ourselves a specific (sell) date, we would expect that it will take several months. It is a large investment," he said.
Pioneer and Caltex merged their petroleum refining and marketing businesses in May 1995 and predicted synergistic savings from the venture of about A$500 million.

Other refiners in Australia are Mobil Corp, Shell Australia and British Petroleum Co Plc but each would face steep regulatory hurdles if they wanted to acquire a half share of Ampol, which has refineries in Sydney and Brisbane.
Schubert said the Ampol venture had already yielded much of the benefits anticipated, and the company now expected the synergy benefits to total about A$600 million.
Pioneer said it anticipated that its second half earnings would be slightly lower than the first half and saw its full year profit materially lower than 1995/96 net earnings of A$258.3 million.
"Ampol's profit performance represents the major uncertainty in the outlook," the company said.
Pioneer said the outlook for Ampol was for continuing poor refiner margins and tough competition in retail markets.
It saw little improvement in the level of dividends from Ampol in the second half despite improving efficiencies and reducing operating costs.

Scubert said the company was starting to see what it expected to be a significant improvement for its Australian building products business which would help lift the company's bottom line in the 1997/98 financial year.
"In addition we are going to see continuing growth in Asia and the benefits of our capital expenditure program (in Europe and America) that is well on the way," Schubert said.
Schubert said Pioneer was on track to spend A$250 million on capital expenditure this financial year to expand its core building materials operations around the world.

He said the company had developed or acquired new quarries in the U.K., Israel, Spain, the Czech Republic, Hong Kong and Thailand and had expanded its pre-mix concrete activities in the Czech Republic, Texas, Thailand and Malaysia.
Pioneer shares closed five cents weaker at A$3.89.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
